sections.heading: Are You Looking for a Trusted Fertilizer Licence Registration in India?
paragraphs: Fertilizers provide robust support for the agriculture of modern farming systems, and a fertilizer licence registration in India is compulsory for any person interested in starting a business that involves selling or distributing fertilizers. The Government of India has provided a regulatory system through which qualified and compliant individuals or businesses undertake trade in fertilizers.

Whether you are an aspiring entrepreneur wanting to have an agricultural fertilizer shop licence or intending to expand into agricultural inputs, this information from Services Plus has everything you need, including how to apply for fertilizer licence registration service, documents required, eligibility criteria, etc.

The fertilizer licence registration in India is a governmental licence to manufacture, sell, import, or distribute fertilizers. As stipulated under the Fertilizer (Control) Act of 1985, no person shall deal in fertilizers unless duly licenced by the state government.

It provides the essential controls on quality, safe handling and storage, and efficient tracking and systems of usage and supply of fertilizers. Whether it is a fertilizer licence registration company in India or just a personal agricultural fertilizer shop, this is the first step to make before embarking on any operations.
There are basically three major licences under the fertilizer licence registration in India:
Manufacturing licence – For those who produce fertilizers.
Wholesale licence – For those selling fertilizers in bulk.
Retail licence – Available for a farmer who sells fertilizers to end users as tenants in fertilizer shop licence.
The categories below are eligible to apply for fertilizer licence registration in India:
Individual entrepreneur
Private Limited and Public Limited Companies
Cooperative societies
Farmers' producers companies
Registered fertilizer dealers or distributors
In India, all new and existing traders and fertilizer licence registration companies must comply with licensing standards before starting fertilizer-related operations.
